survey: A cartoon rocket tilted up and to the right, floating against a sky-blue sunburst background. The red nose cone sits on the silver cylindrical body, with a red rolled rim covering the seam. Two round portholes with blue glass and metal rims are set into the front of the body, one above the other. The lower one looks slightly smaller, which reads as perspective or a design choice. Two red fins are visible near the base, one on the front-left and one on the back-right. Both fins grow straight out of the body's sides, which fits a three- or four-fin layout where the rest are hidden. A short black nozzle ring closes off the bottom of the body, and a small yellow exhaust flame comes straight out of the nozzle. The flame is the rocket's real exhaust, not an invented part. The rocket is shown in flight, so floating with no support is justified. Every part joins the next: nose to rim to body, fins to body, nozzle to body, flame to nozzle. The shapes are round and the counts are plausible.
